sources.citation: Swanton, John R. 1915. Linguistic position of the tribes of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. American Anthropologist n.s. 17(1): 17-40. (Solano vocabulary and comparison pp. 34-36.)
sources.note: No phonology of Solano. Gives the Solano words in a comparison table against Tonkawa, Comecrudo, Cotoname, Coahuilteco, Karankawa, Atakapa; concludes (p. 36) 'Although evidently related to Coahuilteco, the dialect of San Francisco Solano shows that there was considerable divergence'; identifies Solano sa- as a possible 1sg objective prefix. The only prosodic remark in the paper (orthography key, pp. 21-22) concerns Coahuilteco: Garcia's apostrophe marks a preceding consonant 'pronounced with stress, i.e., like a fortis' - nothing about Solano accent. Word forms carry no accent marks.
